    Find an auto repair shop near me, city by city

    Searching for an auto repair shop near me usually returns a wall of ads, map pins and star ratings that are hard to compare. Repair Finder is an independent directory that narrows the field to two kinds of locations: AAA Approved Auto Repair shops and Toyota dealership service centers. Choose a network, type your city or a shop name, and open a page that lists every location we have for that city, with its address, phone number and map.

    Each shop page is built from the details published for that location. Where they are available you will see weekly hours, an open now indicator based on the shop's local time, the repair services offered, the vehicle brands serviced and the AAA member discount the shop lists. Directions open in your maps app, and the Call button dials the shop directly. When a detail is missing, the page leaves it out instead of guessing. You can browse by state or use the search box at the top of this page.

    AAA auto repair shop locator and finder

    If you want an AAA auto repair shop, it helps to know what the badge means. AAA Approved Auto Repair facilities are inspected by AAA and are expected to employ ASE-certified or factory-trained technicians, carry proper insurance, keep a clean and organized facility and earn good customer satisfaction results. AAA also helps resolve disputes between members and approved shops. That is why many drivers treat AAA auto repair as a shortcut to a shop they can trust.

    This page works as an AAA auto repair shop locator and AAA auto repair shop finder for drivers who want a quick list by city. Searching for an AAA auto repair shop near me? Open your city and compare the approved shops side by side. If you need the closest AAA auto repair shop, start with your own city, then check neighboring cities, because shops are grouped by the city in their address. AAA auto service covers far more than roadside help, and approved repair shops are a big part of it. We are independent, so confirm a shop's current status with AAA before you book.

    Benefits vary by AAA club and by shop, so read the AAA auto repair shop discounts on each shop page and ask before you pay. AAA describes a repair warranty of 24 months or 24,000 miles at approved facilities, plus a labor discount for members, commonly 10 percent with a dollar cap that depends on where you live. Show your membership card at the time of service. If AAA auto repair near me returns nothing in a small town, try the next city over.

    Toyota auto repair shops near me

    Many drivers prefer a dealership for warranty work, recalls and model-specific diagnostics. If you are searching for a Toyota auto repair shop near me, our Toyota listings cover dealership service centers across the country. Search Toyota auto repair near me by city, see the address and phone number, and open directions. Toyota auto repair shops near me are not all alike: a dealer service department works from factory procedures and genuine parts, while an independent AAA approved shop often costs less for routine jobs.

    For Toyota auto repair services such as scheduled maintenance, brakes, batteries, hybrid system checks and recall work, call the dealer first and ask about price, wait time and whether you need an appointment. Not near a dealership? Many AAA shops service Toyota vehicles, and the vehicles serviced list on each shop page shows which brands the shop works on. Whichever you pick, a Toyota auto repair shop with certified technicians and a written warranty is a safe bet, and Toyota auto repair is easier to budget for when you compare two estimates.

    How to choose a good auto repair shop near me

    A good auto repair shop near me explains the problem clearly, gives you a written estimate and stands behind its work. Whether you are hunting for the best auto repair shop near me or a cheap auto repair shop near me, the same checklist applies.

    • Check certifications. A certified auto repair shop near me should employ ASE-certified or factory-trained technicians for the work you need.
    • Ask about the warranty. Twelve months and 12,000 miles is a common minimum, and AAA approved shops advertise 24 months or 24,000 miles.
    • Get the estimate in writing, with parts and labor listed separately, and ask the shop to call before doing extra work.
    • Compare two quotes for any job over a few hundred dollars. The lowest price is not always the best value if the repair fails in three months.
    • Read recent reviews on independent sites and look at how the shop handles problems, not only the star rating.

    We do not rank shops or publish prices, so you will not find a best or cheapest label here. You will find the same set of facts for every location, which makes it easier to compare and decide.

    Open now, mobile and do-it-yourself shops

    Auto repair shop near me open now is one of the most common searches. On shop pages that list hours, we show whether the shop is open right now and when it closes or opens next, using the shop's own time zone rather than yours. Hours come from the listing and can change on holidays, so call before you drive over.

    Two other searches deserve an honest note. A mobile auto repair shop near me, meaning a mechanic who comes to your driveway, can handle batteries, brakes and basic diagnostics, but mobile mechanics are not part of this directory. A do it yourself auto repair shop near me, usually a rent-a-bay garage with lifts and tools, is not listed here either. Both can work for simple jobs. For complex repairs, warranty claims or anything safety related, a full-service shop with certified technicians is usually the safer choice.

    Transmission, AC and electrical repairs

    Shop pages list the repair services each location reports, such as air conditioning, brakes, electrical, cooling and radiator, steering and suspension, tires, oil changes and manual or automatic transmissions. If you need a transmission auto repair shop near me, an AC auto repair shop near me or an electrical auto repair shop near me, open your city page and check the services on each shop page before you call. Specialist work such as transmission rebuilds and electrical diagnosis is not offered everywhere, so one quick call can save a wasted trip.

    Own a shop? The AAA auto repair shop application

    Shop owners often ask about the AAA auto repair shop application. Approval is handled by AAA and your regional AAA club, not by this site, and it involves an on-site inspection, technician certifications and customer feedback. Contact your local AAA club to start. Each page on this site shows when its details were last checked.

    Frequently asked questions about auto repair shops

    AAA Approved Auto Repair

    Is Firestone AAA approved?

    Some Firestone Complete Auto Care locations are AAA Approved Auto Repair facilities, but approval is granted shop by shop, not to the whole chain. A Firestone in one city may be approved while another nearby is not. Check the specific location on a city page here or in AAA's official facility locator, and look for the AAA Approved Auto Repair sign at the shop.

    What does referral to AAA approved auto repair facilities mean?

    It means AAA points members to shops it has inspected and approved against its standards instead of recommending random listings. Approved shops are expected to have ASE-certified or factory-trained technicians, proper insurance, a clean facility and good customer satisfaction results, and they agree to AAA's repair warranty and member terms. A referral does not guarantee the outcome of any single repair, so still get a written estimate.

    Does AAA fix engine problems?

    AAA itself does not repair engines. Roadside assistance can handle minor fixes at the curb, such as a dead battery or a flat tire, and can tow you to a shop if the problem is bigger. An AAA Approved Auto Repair facility can diagnose and repair engine problems. Look for minor engine repair, engine overhaul or replacement and gas engine diagnostics in each shop's list of services.

    Does AAA cover mechanical failure?

    No. A standard AAA membership covers roadside services such as towing, battery service and lockouts, not the cost of repairing a mechanical failure. Repair bills are paid by you, by a manufacturer or extended warranty, or by a separate mechanical breakdown policy. AAA approved shops do back their own work with a repair warranty, described by AAA as 24 months or 24,000 miles unless stated otherwise.

    What are the benefits of choosing an AAA approved auto repair shop?

    Approved shops are inspected and vetted for technician certification, insurance, facility standards and customer satisfaction. Members typically get a labor discount, often 10 percent with a maximum that varies by area, a 24-month or 24,000-mile repair warranty and AAA's help resolving disputes. Some shops also offer priority service for towed vehicles and help arranging alternate transportation. Benefits differ by club and by shop, so confirm the details on the shop's page.

    Is AAA auto repair expensive?

    AAA does not set prices. Each approved shop sets its own rates, so costs depend on the shop, your area and the repair. Approved shops are not automatically cheaper or more expensive than independents. The member labor discount can lower the bill and the repair warranty can save money later. Get a written estimate that lists parts and labor, and compare two quotes for larger jobs.

    How do I find a good mechanic?

    Ask for ASE-certified or factory-trained technicians, a written estimate and a warranty; at least 12 months or 12,000 miles is a common minimum. Read recent reviews to see how the shop handles problems, ask friends for recommendations and start with a small job such as an oil change to judge communication. On this site, open your city and choose from AAA approved shops or Toyota dealership service centers.

    Toyota Auto Repair

    Can I service my Toyota at any mechanic?

    Yes. In the United States you can generally have routine maintenance and repairs done at any qualified shop without voiding your new-vehicle warranty, as long as the work is done properly and you keep your records. Warranty repairs, recalls and some software or hybrid-system work are best done at a Toyota dealership, where covered work is free of charge.

    Can a general mechanic work on Toyotas?

    Yes. Most Toyota systems use standard technology, and many independent and AAA approved shops service Toyotas every day. Choose a shop with ASE-certified technicians and the right scan tools. If you drive a hybrid such as a Prius, ask whether the shop works on hybrid systems, since they need extra training and safety procedures. The vehicles serviced list on a shop page shows which brands it handles.

    Are Toyotas expensive to repair?

    Toyotas are generally considered affordable to maintain and repair compared with many brands, because parts are widely available and the models have long track records. Costs still vary. Hybrids, trucks and newer models with advanced safety systems can cost more, and dealership labor rates are usually higher than independent shops. Getting two estimates is the best way to learn what your repair should cost.

    How much does Toyota charge to run a diagnostic?

    It varies by dealership and by problem. A basic check engine scan at many dealers falls roughly between $90 and $150, and intermittent or electrical problems can cost more because they take longer to trace. Many dealerships credit the diagnostic fee toward the repair if you approve it. Ask for the fee and what it includes before you drop off the car.

    What is the most common issue with Toyota?

    It depends on the model and year, so there is no single answer. Commonly reported issues across Toyota models include oil consumption on certain older four-cylinder engines, shifting complaints on some transmissions, brake wear, fuel pump recalls on some models and frame rust on older trucks and SUVs. Check your VIN for open recalls on NHTSA's website and keep up with scheduled maintenance.

    What year to stay away from Toyota?

    No single year is bad for the whole brand, because reliability depends on the model and engine. Owner complaint data and reviews often flag specific combinations, such as models with the 2AZ-FE four-cylinder engine from the 2000s, which is known for oil consumption, and some early-2000s Tacoma and 4Runner trucks with frame rust. Before buying used, run a VIN check for recalls and get a pre-purchase inspection from a shop you trust.

    Which Toyota has the least problems?

    No Toyota is problem free, and rankings change from year to year. Models such as the Corolla, Camry, RAV4 and Prius are often cited as dependable, but results depend on the model year, mileage and how well the car was maintained. Compare the exact model year in owner complaint and recall databases before you buy.

    What car is Toyota discontinuing in 2026?

    The most notable one is the GR Supra. Toyota is ending production of the current-generation sports car with the 2026 model year, closing the run with a limited Final Edition, after the shared platform it used with BMW's Z4 came to an end. Production plans can change, so ask a dealer about current availability and parts support.

    What car is Toyota getting rid of?

    Based on current reports, the GR Supra is the Toyota model ending after 2026. Automakers also retire models at other times for sales and regulatory reasons, so check Toyota's official site or a local dealer for the latest news. A discontinued model can still be serviced: automakers typically keep supplying parts for years, and any qualified shop can maintain it.

    What is the $3000 rule for car repairs?

    It is an informal rule of thumb, not an official rule. If a single repair costs more than about $3,000, or you have spent that much on the same car in a year, it is time to compare repairing against replacing the vehicle. Many people pair it with the 50 percent rule, which suggests replacing a car when a repair costs more than half its market value. Your car's value, mileage and reliability matter more than any single number.

    Shortlist, verify, then test. Shortlist two or three shops from your city page. Verify technician certifications, warranty terms and recent reviews. Then test with a small job or a diagnostic quote before committing to a major repair, and keep written estimates and invoices.

    Where can I find AAA auto repair shops near me?

    Choose the AAA Approved network on this site, search your city or browse by state, and open the city page to see every AAA approved shop we list there with its address, phone number, hours and member discount. You can also use AAA's official facility locator to confirm a shop's current status.

    Who provides expert auto repair services near me?

    Look for shops with ASE-certified or factory-trained technicians. AAA approved shops are expected to have certified or factory-trained staff for the services they offer, and Toyota dealership service centers typically use factory-trained technicians for Toyota vehicles. Check a shop's services list and ask which certifications the technician working on your car holds.

    Where can I find quality auto repair near me?

    Quality signs include technician certifications, a written warranty, a clean and organized facility and steady customer feedback. AAA's approval process checks several of these, and dealership service centers follow manufacturer standards. Use the city pages to shortlist, then verify with recent reviews.

    How do I choose an auto repair shop near me in Miami?

    Start with the Miami, FL city page. Shortlist shops that are AAA approved or Toyota dealerships, check their services, hours and vehicles serviced, then call two or three for written estimates. Florida has consumer rules for motor vehicle repair, so ask for an estimate in writing and keep your paperwork.

    Is there a good auto engine repair shop near me?

    Check the services on each shop page for minor engine repair, engine overhaul or replacement and gas engine diagnostics. Not every shop does major engine work, so call to confirm they handle your engine type, and ask for a diagnostic and a written estimate. For a big repair, compare the cost with your car's value, as described in the $3,000 rule above.

    Who accepts Sunbit near me for auto repair?

    Sunbit is a point-of-sale financing company, and each shop decides whether to accept it, so we cannot list who does. Ask the shop before you book, or check with Sunbit directly. Also ask about other payment options, such as an installment plan from the shop or a credit card.

    Who does auto glass repair near me?

    Auto glass is a separate specialty from mechanical repair. AAA's facility locator has an auto glass facility type, and some general repair shops list auto glass among their services. Our listings focus on mechanical repair shops and Toyota dealerships, so call a shop to confirm before you go, and check your insurance policy, since glass coverage is common.
